page: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 124 GB of system memory, delivering a dense ratio of 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The configuration includes no discrete graphics hardware or accelerators and comes with no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for the operating system and data retention. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary hardware characteristic of this profile is its high memory-to-core density. Because compute allocation is moderate compared to the extensive memory footprint, the instance is cost-efficient for setups constrained by memory capacity rather than CPU cycles. This architecture avoids the expense of over-provisioning extra compute cores simply to secure high memory capacities. The primary tradeoff is the total reliance on external persistent storage and bounded multithreaded compute throughput defined by the 8 dedicated vCPUs.

Given this hardware profile, m4-hypermem-8 is tailored for workloads requiring significant memory allocation with modest processing demands. Typical use cases include in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes such as Redis or Memcached, real-time memory-resident analytics, and enterprise data services managing large working datasets in active memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for applications requiring high memory capacity relative to compute resources. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 124 GB of memory, yielding 15.5 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration features no local storage and zero GPU accelerators, necessitating external block storage for system files and persistent data. This profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound systems by avoiding the overhead of provisioning unneeded processor cores to access large RAM arrays. The operational tradeoff lies in its dependence on network-attached storage and an 8-core CPU threshold. Consequently, the m4-hypermem-8 instance is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, memory-resident analytics, and enterprise applications managing high-volume data structures resident in RAM.
